caveats: TISCH2 values are precomputed means; no per-cell distributions or differential-expression statistics.
One dataset (PAAD_GSE162708) shows inverted fibroblast/malignant ordering for EGFR/ERBB2 — likely an annotation artifact; the cross-dataset mean is robust to it.
Baseline expression is not inducibility. This only clears the prerequisite; the actual upregulation must be tested in the daraxonrasib-treated CAF time course.
analyses.figure_caption: Mean log-normalized expression of EGFR, MET, ERBB2, ERBB3 in fibroblasts vs malignant cells across TISCH2 PAAD datasets.
findings: All four RTKs (EGFR, MET, ERBB2, ERBB3) are detectable in fibroblasts across 7–9 independent human PDAC scRNA-seq datasets.
Expression is consistently lower than in malignant cells: EGFR 2.3× lower, ERBB2 2.6× lower, ERBB3 23× lower, MET 20× lower (mean log-normalized values).
EGFR and ERBB2 have the most robust baseline fibroblast signal (present in every dataset) — the best candidates for testing the CAF-upregulation hypothesis in vitro.
MET and ERBB3 sit near the detection floor in fibroblasts, so any treatment-induced fold change there would need high-sensitivity assays to see.
analyses.question: Daraxonrasib upregulates EGFR, MET, ERBB2/HER2 and ERBB3 on PDAC tumor cells. Step zero for a resistant-CAF hypothesis: do cancer-associated fibroblasts express these receptors at all in untreated human PDAC?
analyses.summary: Baseline receptor check across 7–9 human PDAC scRNA-seq datasets (TISCH2). All four RTKs are detectable in fibroblasts, consistently below malignant-cell levels (2–23× lower). EGFR and ERBB2 have the most robust fibroblast signal; MET and ERBB3 are barely detectable.
analyses.title: Do PDAC CAFs express the daraxonrasib-induced RTKs?

caveats: Power is computed from observed (post-hoc) effect sizes — optimistic for the big hits, which is why the recommendation is to reduce replicates there rather than claim a powered discovery.
Log2 t-test assumes roughly log-normal data; reasonable for ELISA concentrations in range.
The BU line's DMSO and all BU treatments sit near the assay floor, so fold changes there are noisy.
findings: The 100 nM 5-day hits (AZ 15.1×, GOL 205 20.1×, GOL 321 2.6×) are at ~100% power with triplicates; they can be run at n=2–3.
The GOL 321 'weak' 2.6× effect is not weak for power purposes — its triplicates were tight (SD 0.11 on log2 scale), so n=2–3 already detects it.

AZ 10 nM daily is the expensive condition (n=11 for 80% power) because of high-CV triplicates — cleaner technicals or dropping it saves the most wells. GOL 205 10 nM 5-day needs n=25 (small 1.6× effect, moderate variance).
GOL 321 10 nM daily ('n=24') is not a real design target: one near-zero replicate explodes the log2 SD, so powering against that outlier is meaningless. Re-run cleanly or exclude.
BU 5-day conditions are flat (0.88–0.91×) — powered to detect nothing; keep only as controls. GOL 205 10 nM daily reads zero (assay floor, no variance to power against).
analyses.question: The first IL-6 ELISA round showed strong daraxonrasib-driven IL-6 induction in some CAF lines/conditions and noisy flat ones in others. How many replicates per condition does the repeat need for 80% power?
analyses.summary: Two-sample t-test on log2 concentrations (α = 0.05, 80% power, conservative variance). The three 100 nM 5-day hits are already saturated at triplicates — run them at n=2–3 and spend plate space on the noisy daily-dose conditions (AZ 10 nM daily needs n=11). The constraint is noise, not effect size.
analyses.title: IL-6 ELISA: sizing the repeat (power analysis)

caveats: Mean z-score on bulk TPM is fine for condition contrasts, not a per-cell classifier; a rank method is provided for scRNA-seq inputs.
The iCAF signature is the weakest link here (6 mouse genes; Il6/Has1 near-zero in vitro at 32 h) — scores track Cxcl1/Ly6c1/Col14a1.
v1 myCAF/iCAF/apCAF markers are the main-text core sets from Elyada 2019; a v2 could expand from the full DE tables.
analyses.figure_caption: Signature scores by condition in GSE291118 (myCAF, iCAF, SASP, matrisome, MAPK output across the four treatment arms).
findings: Macropinocytosis blockade under metabolic stress drives myCAF→iCAF transition plus stromal remodeling (EIPA vs vehicle): myCAF down, SASP up, MAPK-output up, matrisome down, apCAF up — all at p=0.0079 (minimum achievable with n=5/group). Gene-level: Acta2 533→108 TPM, Col1a1 675→262 TPM.

Metabolic stress alone induces the iCAF program only partially: it erodes myCAF identity (p=0.0079) but dampens baseline inflammatory transcripts (iCAF/SASP down) at the 32 h bulk timepoint. The inflammatory gain appears only once the macropinocytosis brake is removed — consistent with the paper's own model.
IL-1α positive control passed (iCAF up p=0.0079, SASP up p=0.0159), validating the scorer against the canonical iCAF inducer.
Gene coverage on the matrix: 6/6 myCAF, 6/6 iCAF, 5/5 apCAF, 19/19 matrisome, 9/9 MAPK, 7/7 RAS-ON PD, 13/14 SASP.
Plot twist worth knowing: GSE291118 is not a KRAS-inhibitor dataset — it's about metabolic stress and macropinocytosis in CAFs. The MAPK/RAS-ON signatures are the bridge to the daraxonrasib work.
analyses.question: Can we build a versioned, citable set of CAF-subtype and RAS-inhibition signatures, validate a reusable scorer, and reproduce a published CAF-subtype result with it?
analyses.summary: Built signatures_v1.yaml (7 signatures: myCAF, iCAF, apCAF, SASP, core matrisome, MAPK output, RAS(ON)-inhibition PD readout) with PubMed-verified provenance, plus a reusable CLI scorer. Validated by reproducing Zhang et al., Cancer Cell 2025 (GSE291118): blocking macropinocytosis drives the myCAF→iCAF transition exactly as reported, and the IL-1α positive control confirms the scorer. One claim reproduced only partially — reported honestly.
analyses.title: CAF signature compendium + GSE291118 reproduction

caveats: The NEJM phase 1/2 trial paper's data-sharing statement is unverified (subscription-only).
Publication links for the newest deposits were verified 2026-09-18; re-verify before reuse in a thesis.
GSE336609 (appendiceal PDX, normal→iCAF shift after KRAS inhibition) withholds raw data for patient privacy — processed only.
findings: No public omics of daraxonrasib-resistant PDAC exists. The flagship resistance paper (Aronchik et al., Nature Medicine, Aug 2026) deposited only 2 WES samples (parental vs resistant HPAC xenografts) as MAF files — the 44-patient ctDNA data are not deposited anywhere.

Nothing is under controlled access: the paper's data-availability statement mentions no dbGaP/EGA. Patient data availability is deferred to the NEJM phase 1/2 trial paper (unverified, likely sponsor-mediated).
Best public PDAC comparator: GSE269985 — multi-model KRAS-inhibitor resistance (MRTX1133) with KRAS/MYC/MET/EGFR/CDK6 amps, EMT and PI3K themes mirroring daraxonrasib resistance.
Best dataset for her CAF angle: GSE337208 — in vivo KPC scRNA-seq under RMC-6236 with stromal/CAF populations intact (short-term treatment, not resistance).
Only true RMC-6236-resistant line with omics found: GSE324125 (H358 NSCLC) — usable as a RAS(ON)-resistance expression signature, wrong tissue.
analyses.question: Is there a public omics dataset of daraxonrasib-resistant PDAC that can serve as the tumor-cell comparator for the resistance chapter — or must resistant Capan-1/KP-4 lines be generated?
analyses.summary: Searched GEO, ArrayExpress and ENA (269 raw hits, 16 curated datasets). Verdict: no public omics of daraxonrasib-resistant PDAC exists — generating her own resistant lines is justified and fills a genuine gap. The flagship Aronchik et al., Nature Medicine 2026 paper deposited only 2 WES samples; nothing sits under controlled access. Best free comparator: GSE269985 (multi-model PDAC KRAS-inhibitor resistance). Best CAF-angle dataset: GSE337208 (RMC-6236-treated KPC scRNA-seq with stromal populations).
analyses.title: Daraxonrasib resistance datasets: what exists publicly?
Mining GSE337208: CAF subtype shifts under RMC-6236
analyses.question: Does RMC-6236 remodel CAF subtype identity (myCAF/iCAF/apCAF, SASP, matrisome) in vivo? Scoring the KPC single-cell fibroblasts from GSE337208 (Mahadevan et al., Nat Commun 2026) with the validated signature panel.
analyses.summary: Scored fibroblast/CAF cells from murine KPC PDAC (GSE337208, Mahadevan et al., Nat Commun 2026) treated with RMC-6236 or MRTX1133 ± immunotherapy, using the repo's validated signature scorer. RMC-6236 pushes CAFs myCAF→iCAF/apCAF in vivo, but the drug's own MAPK pharmacodynamic readout doesn't register in fibroblasts — the reprogramming looks indirect. Combination arms nearly erased the captured fibroblast compartment.
findings: Primary contrast (KPC2 RMC-6236 vs vehicle, 53 vs 42 fibroblasts, per-cell Mann–Whitney U): myCAF down (p=0.012), iCAF up (p=0.0005), apCAF up (p=0.0002) — the myCAF→iCAF direction now shown in PDAC itself, matching the appendiceal KRAS-inhibition precedent (GSE336609).

The drug's MAPK pharmacodynamic readout (Dusp6/Spry/Etv) did not move in fibroblasts at day 14 — CAF reprogramming here is likely indirect (tumor-cell signaling or microenvironmental cues), not direct MAPK suppression in CAFs.

Stromal collapse: fibroblast fraction fell 15.9%→2.6% under MRTX1133, and the RMC-6236+anti-CTLA4 / +anti-PD1 arms captured zero fibroblasts. Depletion vs dissociation bias is unresolvable at n=1 — a methods warning for her own combination experiments.
Secondary: MRTX1133+anti-CTLA4 suppressed apCAF/MAPK/PD signatures in the remaining fibroblasts (KPC3).
Genuine extension: the Mahadevan et al. paper is T-cell-centric — the fibroblast compartment was never scored, so this analysis adds something the paper didn't.
caveats: n=1 sample per arm: cell-level p-values are pseudoreplicated; no sample-level inference is possible.
Fibroblasts identified heuristically (k-means on a 16-gene panel); the study provides no author cell annotations.
iCAF genes are sparsely detected in scRNA-seq (the signature panel's known weak link) — the iCAF score rides on few genes per cell.
10–14 day treatment = short-term response, not acquired resistance.
Zero fibroblasts captured in the combo arms — stromal depletion vs dissociation artifact cannot be distinguished here.
analyses.figure_caption: Per-cell signature scores in KPC2 fibroblasts, RMC-6236 vs vehicle (53 vs 42 cells): myCAF down, iCAF and apCAF up.
